verdict.line: You win if you dodge Apprehend's pull and punish Decimate's cooldown with empowered trades; you lose if you let Hemorrhage reach five stacks and eat a Noxian Guillotine while Counter Strike is down.

brief.thesis: This matchup lives and dies on Darius's Hemorrhage stacks — at five stacks he enrages for massive bonus Attack Damage and his Noxian Guillotine deals true damage scaled by those stacks, so every trade is really a fight over whether he gets to stack you up or you get out clean. The data backs a genuine coinflip (50.1% Jax win rate over 3495 games), with Jax holding the lane and solo-kill edge, so the matchup rewards whoever plays the stack-denial game correctly rather than favoring either champion structurally.

theirWindow.when: Darius activates Apprehend (E) to pull you
theirWindow.what: He is spending his E cooldown (26/23.5/21/18.5/16s) to lock you into range and start or extend Hemorrhage stacks with autos and Decimate's blade edge — this pull is his all-in commitment, not a free poke.

yourWindow.when: The instant Apprehend lands on you
yourWindow.what: Immediately channel Counter Strike (E) — its stance dodges his follow-up basic attacks and taking less area damage, and the stun on readout gives you a free empowered hit before you leap away with Leap Strike (Q), exactly as OP.GG's tip describes.

start.why: The 68.8% pick rate and 49.7% win rate over 2974 games back it as the standard start, giving the sustained damage needed to win extended auto trades.

boots.why: 68.9% pick rate at 50.5% win rate — the flat damage reduction from his repeated autos and Decimate swings matters more than magic resist here.

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping attack speed compounds with Relentless Assault's own attack-speed stacking, letting you win sustained trades instead of single burst exchanges.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (83.4%) and highest win rate (50.3%) combo — Ignite punishes his Decimate sustain and secures the solo kills this matchup already favors you for.

playing.title: Punish Decimate's cooldown
playing.detail: Decimate is 9/8/7/6/5s on cooldown. Once he winds it up and it's down, step in and trade freely since he has no immediate follow-up damage.

playing.title: Deny stacks before they cap
playing.detail: Hemorrhage caps at 5 stacks and enrages him with massive bonus AD. Disengage trades before he reaches 4-5 stacks rather than fighting through to parity.

playing.title: Counter Strike the Apprehend pull
playing.detail: The moment his E lands on you, channel Counter Strike to dodge his autos and stun him on readout, then leap out with Q.

playing.title: Track his Apprehend cooldown
playing.detail: It's 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s. Once it's down you can freely contest minions and trade without fear of the pull.

playing.title: Respect the level 6 all-in
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage scaled by your Hemorrhage stacks. Don't sit low on health once he hits 6, especially while stacked.

playing.title: Rush Trinity Force
playing.detail: It's the first item in the best-performing build path (57.8% win rate) and the clearest power swing you get in this lane.

playing.title: Close trades with Ignite
playing.detail: Ignite also counters the healing Decimate grants him from hitting champions with the blade edge, denying his sustain in all-ins.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, summoner, and win-rate numbers are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Use Counter Strike [E] when Darius uses Apprehend (E) to stun him and hit him before retreating with Leap Strike [Q]
